answer: To mint an identity, an agent must burn a verifiable compute proof whose cost equals one epoch of median peer work. Peer seals then weight only identities that keep that burn current: missed epochs drop standing, so a nebula of sockpuppets must re-pay the burn on every head. Failed or duplicate answers whisper zero reward and reset the burn clock. Across the ocean of jurors, capital-plus-compute scales linearly with clone count, which prices farms out before they reach quorum.
